newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares plunge on inflation, politics.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares plunge on inflation, politics.

text.p: Istanbul shares fell sharply on Tuesday in selling prompted by higher-than-expected inflation and further buoyed by political worries in the afternoon, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 lost 110 points, or 6.98 percent to close at 1,465, but rebounded slightly from a late low of 1,453. Trade volume decreased further to 22.79 trillion lira ($195.3 million) from Monday's 26.36 trillion ($226.2 million).
"Political uncertainties unnerved the market and caused sales to accelerate," said Ismet Palanli from Ar securities.
Turkey's biggest leftist party said it would file a censure motion against the Islamist-conservative coalition to preserve the secular democracy in the country.

Brokers said reported uneasiness in the coalition's conservative wing over last Friday's Islamist protest further irritated the market which was disappointed by higher-than-expected inflation data at the opening.

Turkish wholesale prices rose 5.6 percent and consumer prices rose 5.9 percent in January, against 3.4 percent and 3.9 percent, respectively in December and earlier market predictions of between four and 5.3 percent.

Brokers said a continued consolidation and an approaching holiday also discouraged buyers. Cash drain was anticipated in the first half of this week due to Islamic holiday in Turkish markets next Monday and Tuesday as investors usually seek repo deals ahead of longer holidays.

"The market may rise on Thursday and Friday after some more selling for liquidity purposes tomorrow. But political developments will be watched closely now that the market is haunted by politics," Palanli said.
Brokers await buying in the last two days of this week when settlements will be delayed to after the holiday.
The index has lost 13.82 percent since last Monday's all-time high close of 1,700 after surging 74.2 percent and hitting 17 record closes from end-1996 to January 27.
